subject.title: fix(network): guarded redirects survive cleanup rejection

question: Should this protected maintainer-labelled guarded-fetch fix require production-entry runtime proof in addition to the native-stream regression before it is merged?
rationale: The implementation appears bounded, but suppressing a cleanup rejection on a shared network path is intentional behavior that needs an owner to accept the proof standard and non-authoritative cleanup contract.

options.title: Request runtime proof
options.body: Ask for redacted after-fix terminal or runtime output through the guarded-fetch entry point, showing the successful second hop and absence of an unhandled rejection.

options.title: Accept current regression evidence
options.body: Treat the native-stream regression and completed focused CI as sufficient evidence for this small cleanup-only change.

recommendation.title: Request runtime proof
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted after-fix terminal or runtime output through the guarded-fetch entry point, showing the successful second hop and absence of an unhandled rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: The current author is the most direct routing candidate for the focused shared-path follow-up and any additional proof.
